From 666c53e94c1d0bf0bdf14c49505ece9ddbe725bc Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Jared Kangas <jkangas@redhat.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 11:46:50 -0800
Subject: [PATCH] dmaengine: fsl-edma: don't explicitly disable clocks in
 .remove()

The clocks in fsl_edma_engine::muxclk are allocated and enabled with
devm_clk_get_enabled(), which automatically cleans these resources up,
but these clocks are also manually disabled in fsl_edma_remove(). This
causes warnings on driver removal for each clock:

        edma_module already disabled
        WARNING: CPU: 0 PID: 418 at drivers/clk/clk.c:1200 clk_core_disable+0x198/0x1c8
        [...]
        Call trace:
         clk_core_disable+0x198/0x1c8 (P)
         clk_disable+0x34/0x58
         fsl_edma_remove+0x74/0xe8 [fsl_edma]
         [...]
        
diff --git a/drivers/dma/fsl-edma-main.c b/drivers/dma/fsl-edma-main.c
index a753b7cbfa7a..dbcdd1e68319 100644
--- a/drivers/dma/fsl-edma-main.c
+++ b/drivers/dma/fsl-edma-main.c
@@ -915,7 +915,6 @@ static void fsl_edma_remove(struct platform_device *pdev)
 	of_dma_controller_free(np);
 	dma_async_device_unregister(&fsl_edma->dma_dev);
 	fsl_edma_cleanup_vchan(&fsl_edma->dma_dev);
-	fsl_disable_clocks(fsl_edma, fsl_edma->drvdata->dmamuxs);
 }
 
 static int fsl_edma_suspend_late(struct device *dev)
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary

**Modified file:** `drivers/dma/fsl-edma-main.c`

**Change:**  
Removed the call to `fsl_disable_clocks(fsl_edma, fsl_edma->drvdata->dmamuxs);` from the `fsl_edma_remove()` function.

**Relationship to the bug:**  
The clocks in `fsl_edma_engine::muxclk` were previously allocated and enabled via `devm_clk_get_enabled()`, which automatically handles resource cleanup, including disabling clocks when the device is removed. However, the remove function explicitly disabled these same clocks, resulting in a double-disable operation. This caused a kernel warning (`edma_module already disabled`) and a call trace in the clock core. By removing the redundant manual disable, the patches prevent the warning and ensure proper cleanup via the devres mechanism.

dmaengine: fsl-edma: don't explicitly disable clocks in

The clocks in fsl_edma_engine::muxclk are allocated and enabled with
devm_clk_get_enabled(), which automatically cleans these resources up,
but these clocks are also manually disabled in fsl_edma_remove(). This
causes warnings on driver removal for each clock:

        edma_module already disabled
        WARNING: CPU: 0 PID: 418 at drivers/clk/clk.c:1200 clk_core_disable+0x198/0x1c8
        [...]

         clk_core_disable+0x198/0x1c8 (P)
         clk_disable+0x34/0x58
         fsl_edma_remove+0x74/0xe8 [fsl_edma]
         [...]
        ---[ end trace 0000000000000000 ]---
        edma_module already unprepared
        WARNING: CPU: 0 PID: 418 at drivers/clk/clk.c:1059 clk_core_unprepare+0x1f8/0x220
        [...]

         fsl_edma_remove+0x7c/0xe8 [fsl_edma]
         [...]
        ---[ end trace 0000000000000000 ]---

Fix these warnings by removing the unnecessary fsl_disable_clocks() call
in fsl_edma_remove().

Fixes: a9903de3aa16 ("dmaengine: fsl-edma: refactor using devm_clk_get_enabled")
Signed-off-by: Jared Kangas <jkangas@redhat.com>
Reviewed-by: Frank Li <Frank.Li@nxp.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260113-fsl-edma-clock-removal-v1-1-2025b49e7bcc@redhat.com
Signed-off-by: Vinod Koul <vkoul@kernel.org>

Here is the root cause:
The clocks are allocated with devm_clk_get_enabled() which automatically disables them on driver removal, but the .remove() callback also manually disables them, causing a double-disable and a kernel warning.

Here is the patch:
 
 static void fsl_edma_remove(struct platform_device *pdev)
 {
 	struct device_node *np = pdev->dev.of_node;
 	struct fsl_edma_engine *fsl_edma = platform_get_drvdata(pdev);
 
 	fsl_edma_irq_exit(pdev, fsl_edma);
 	of_dma_controller_free(np);
 	dma_async_device_unregister(&fsl_edma->dma_dev);
 	fsl_edma_cleanup_vchan(&fsl_edma->dma_dev);
-	fsl_disable_clocks(fsl_edma, fsl_edma->drvdata->dmamuxs);
 }

The code statements that lead to the bug are:

```c

```
```c
fsl_disable_clocks(fsl_edma, fsl_edma->drvdata->dmamuxs);
```

**Reason:**  
The clocks are acquired with `devm_clk_get_enabled()`, which ensures they are automatically disabled and unprepared when the device is removed. However, `fsl_edma_remove()` additionally calls `fsl_disable_clocks()`, causing a double disable for each clock, leading to the kernel warnings about "already disabled" and "already unprepared".

---

The code statements that fix the bug are:

```c
-	fsl_disable_clocks(fsl_edma, fsl_edma->drvdata->dmamuxs);
```

**Reason:**  
Removing the manual `fsl_disable_clocks()` call eliminates the double-disabling. The clocks are still safely cleaned up by the devres framework because they were allocated with `devm_clk_get_enabled()`, so the warnings are avoided without affecting functionality.
